about: Closed vocabularies for coding one evidence entry as one or more cells: learners in state L, working on a goal with properties G, under conditions C, changing design variable D, measured on outcome O. '?' means the study's text available here does not say; it is never a default and never read as any other value.

knowledge_type.concept: categories and their features; recognising instances
knowledge_type.procedure: a step sequence to carry out (solving an equation type, a clinical check)
knowledge_type.principle: rules, causal models, explanations that must be understood to be applied
knowledge_type.complex-skill: whole-task performance integrating several of the above (troubleshooting, speaking, writing, clinical care)
knowledge_type.attitude-motivation: interest, beliefs, self-efficacy, dispositions as the target

element_interactivity.low: elements can be learned one at a time
element_interactivity.high: elements must be processed together to be understood
element_interactivity.?: not stated or not inferable from the text

expertise.novice: little or no prior knowledge of the target
expertise.mixed: the sample spans levels, or results are reported across levels

setting.classroom: school or university class with a teacher
setting.online-instructor-led: digital with a live instructor or cohort

duration.days-weeks: several sessions over up to about two months

variable.example-problem-sequencing: order or pairing of examples and problems
variable.fading: gradually removing worked steps or support
variable.scaffolding: support adjusted to the learner, other than fading
variable.feedback-type: what the feedback says (corrective, elaborated, recast, metalinguistic, process-level)
variable.retrieval-practice: testing or recall practice versus restudy or none
variable.spacing: spaced or expanding versus massed schedule
variable.explicit-instruction: explicit or direct instruction versus discovery or implicit
variable.guided-discovery: discovery with guidance versus unguided discovery
variable.formative-assessment: assessment used to adjust teaching or learning
variable.problem-first: problem solving or exploration before instruction (productive failure) versus instruction first
variable.case-comparison: comparing contrasting cases, solution methods, or correct and erroneous examples
variable.prompts: metacognitive, reflection or explanation prompts other than self-explanation of examples
variable.active-learning: active, interactive or peer-discussion formats versus lecture or passive study
variable.praise: praise, and what it targets (person, effort, process)
variable.autonomy-support: choice and autonomy-supportive versus controlling conditions
variable.media-design: pictures, decorative or seductive details, multimedia presentation choices
variable.test-format: format of a practice test (multiple choice, short answer, free recall)
variable.mastery-learning: mastery criteria with corrective loops versus fixed pacing
variable.technology-tool: a specific tool or medium (ASR, video, app) versus another or none
variable.learner-difference: NOT a design choice: a comparison between kinds of learners (high vs low achievers, novices vs experts). Code the learners in L and the contrast here only so it is not lost
variable.other: none of the above; name it in treatment

outcome.delayed-retention: the same material tested after a delay (a day or more)
outcome.learning-time: time or effort to reach a level
outcome.cognitive-load: rated or measured load or effort
outcome.general-achievement: a course, unit or standardised achievement test, or a pooled 'learning' outcome that does not separate retention from transfer
outcome.assessment-accuracy: accuracy or validity of self-, peer- or teacher assessment

direction.+: the treatment did BETTER on this outcome than the comparison (for learning-time and cognitive-load, better means less), reported as significant or with an interval excluding zero
direction.-: the treatment did WORSE (for learning-time and cognitive-load, worse means more)
direction.0: no difference, AND the study reports an equivalence test or adequate power for the effect of interest
direction.ns: no significant difference and no power or equivalence reported: inconclusive, never read as no effect
direction.mixed: differs across subgroups or measures within this cell
direction.?: the text does not show the direction for this outcome

design.within-subject: each learner in every condition, counterbalanced
design.synthesis-experimental: meta-analysis or systematic review of experiments
design.synthesis-mixed: synthesis mixing experimental and non-experimental studies
design.argument: theoretical or narrative, no new data

evidence_status.known: at least one randomised or synthesis-experimental cell for these learners, goal and conditions (all specified axes match)
evidence_status.extrapolated: experimental cells exist, but for learners, goals or conditions that differ on one or more axes
evidence_status.associational: only correlational, qualitative or non-random evidence
